transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-06-07 09:00 PT
- Duration: 00:47:00 (approx)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Leo (SE), Oliver (CSM), Samir (CTO, Equator), Priya (ML Lead), Marco (Infra), Hannah (Compliance), Ethan (SWE)

Summary (auto):
Equator AI is evaluating hosting options across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments for their customer-facing LLM APIs. They currently run a vLLM/TGI-based self-hosted stack on Azure and are exploring an escape hatch due to cost spikes and scale problems. Primary concerns: inference parity w/ OpenAI-like outputs, latency at 50-300ms P95, quantization compatibility, KMS/HSM integration, VPC peering and private control plane, SOC2 + audit logs. Redwood AE (Maya) + SE (Leo) walked through serving model differences, fallback routing, KV cache strategies and proposed a 2-week POC/benchmark. Action items and next steps captured.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining — can you all hear me okay?
[00:03] Samir (Equator CTO): Yep yep, loud and clear.
[00:05] Priya (ML): Good morning.
[00:06] Maya: Great. Quick intro — I run GTM for Redwood inference and Leo our SE is focused on performance and migrations. Oliver from CSM is here to help spin up pilots. Could do a quick round robin please, your roles and must-haves?
[00:18] Samir: Sure — Samir, CTO at Equator. We're responsible for our product infra, we're seeing cost and scale issues as we grow to 10s of thousands of monthly active generators.
[00:26] Priya: Priya, ML lead. We own model stack — currently on vLLM/TGI serving open models, we tune quantized GGML-ish stuff, and want parity vs OpenAI for a bunch of prompt families.
[00:36] Marco: Marco, infra — I manage Azure infra + networking, VNet peerings, private link. Important for us: private control plane and KMS.
[00:44] Hannah: Hannah, compliance — SOC2, logs, SSO via Okta and SAML, and some EU data residency constraints.
[00:51] Maya: Awesome, thanks. High level — can you tell us about your top two pain points right now?
[00:57] Samir: Cost unpredictability and latency spikes under burst. On a normal day p95 is okay but when we spin up batches for batch inference we see token cost shoot and response times jump. Also engineering burden — we have to manage kernel/runtime quirks across GPUs.
[01:14] Priya: And model parity — certain prompts where OpenAI used to be our reference, the output distribution is drifted on our tuned GGML quantized path. We need reproducible evals for quality.
[01:25] Leo (Redwood SE): Got it — so two threads: operational economics/hosting and eval parity. Can you share numbers for p95 latency targets and token cost targets?
[01:34] Priya: Target p95 is sub 300ms for short completions (<=128 tokens), ideally 150-200ms. Cost target is more relative — we want 2x less than our current token-equivalent spend, or at least predictable tail behavior.
[01:45] Maya: Helpful. Marco, on the infra side — are you on single subscription in Azure? Do you have private subnets/VNet peering for customers?
[01:54] Marco: Yes we use multiple subscriptions, private endpoints, and we have a mix of AKS and VMSS for our GPU fleet. We also use Azure Key Vault for keys.
[02:03] Maya: Okay sounds consistent with many customers migrating. Quick question — are you considering Redwood Hosted (fastest onboard), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), or Private (VPC/on-prem)? Any preference?
[02:13] Samir: We want a hybrid path. Start hosted to test parity then move to Dedicated or Private depending on compliance and cost. Hannah will push private for EU production but maybe hosted for non-sensitive traffic.
[02:24] Hannah: Yes that matches compliance constraints. We need audit logs and KMS integration before production.
[02:29] Leo: Totally reasonable. For parity checks we typically run a small benchmark comparing sample prompts across OpenAI, your vLLM/TGI baseline, and our Redwood runtime. We'll measure tokenization differences, logprobs, and output similarity metrics. Does that sound useful?
[02:44] Priya: Yes. What about quantized weights — does Redwood support int8/int4 paths that mirror our GGML tuned models? We've had issues with generation artifacts post-quantize.
[02:53] Leo: We support quantization-friendly execution paths and have profiles for common quantized formats. Two caveats: some pathological prompts surface different tokenization or attention quirks depending on kernel selection, and we can give recommendations for retraining or calibration. We'll include quantization profiles in the benchmark plan.
[03:09] Ethan (SWE): Quick nit — our current stack uses TGI and has custom sampling tweaks (temp annealing) — will those be portable?
[03:16] Leo: Sampling parameters are portable generally — temperature, top-k, top-p — but implementation of fast kernels can change micro-behavior. We'll validate sample-level fidelity in the parity tests.
[03:25] Samir: Another big concern — can Redwood handle our scale for inference fallbacks? We need graceful degradation. If a larger model is slow, we need automatic route to a cheaper variant that maintains quality.
[03:36] Maya: That's core to what we do — smart routing with fallbacks by policy. You can set SLOs and Redwood will route by latency/cost tier, or fallback to a pinned smaller variant when a threshold hits. We'll show routing demo in a follow-up.
[03:49] [small crosstalk]
[03:52] Marco: Networking question — private control plane, does Redwood require inbound peering or do we establish outbound tunnels? Also how does data plane sit with our VNet?
[04:02] Oliver (CSM): Most customers prefer a private deployment with customer-managed VPC peering where the control plane can be private-managed; for hosted we offer a private link option and egress rules. We'll share architecture notes — usually outbound only from your infra to Redwood endpoints is acceptable but for private/on-prem we include an option for air-gapped control plane.
[04:18] Hannah: KMS specifics: can you integrate with Azure Key Vault or bring-your-own HSM? We need envelope encryption and audit trails.
[04:27] Maya: Yes we support BYO KMS/HSM integrations and can enable CMKs in the Dedicated/Private plans. We'll include a security doc with specifics.
[04:35] Priya: On evaluation — what's a realistic timeline for a parity POC? We can provide a 2-3k prompt eval set for the initial sprint.
[04:43] Leo: Typical is 1-2 weeks for an initial parity run: ingest eval corpus, run across OpenAI baseline, your current vLLM/TGI, and Redwood-hosted. Then analyze differences and surface diffs and failure modes. If you want on-prem parity for private deployment it's an extra week to stand up the Private control plane.
[04:59] Samir: That sounds good. Cost — are you competitive with OpenAI for embeddings and completions? Our spend is heavy on completion tokens.
[05:08] Maya: We position to be cost-competitive after factoring in batching, KV caching and quantization. Raw per-token cost varies by model; we'll propose pricing for hosted and a reserved capacity model for Dedicated. The biggest wins come from caching repeated prefixes and optimized batching.
[05:23] Priya: How does Redwood handle KV cache across multi-tenant GPUs? We saw KV cache evictions cause quality problems for conversational flows.
[05:31] Leo: We do a couple things: persistent KV cache for pinned sessions, per-customer cache sharding and heuristics to keep hot prefixes resident. On Dedicated you can pin model shards too which reduces eviction churn. We'll include cache behavior in the benchmark.
[05:46] [pause, typing sounds]
[05:50] Marco: If we go Private, what's the deployment footprint? We are on a mix of A100 and newer H100 GPUs — any constraints?
[05:58] Leo: We target both A100 and H100. Kernel selection and sequence-length tuning will be part of the compatibility notes — some micro-ops are faster on H100. For Private we provide a deployment runbook and resource profiles.
[06:10] Hannah: For compliance we need retention controls and the ability to turn off logs for certain tenants. Is that supported?
[06:17] Oliver: Yes, retention policies at the account/tenant level are configurable, and we can disable or truncate certain logs; for Dedicated and Private customers you can control retention windows and audit forwarding to your SIEM.
[06:30] Priya: One more on eval — how do you compare outputs? BLEU-like metrics? We use a mix of embedding-sim, ROUGE-ish metrics, and human evals.
[06:40] Leo: We look at embedding similarity against OpenAI baseline, perplexity where applicable, and sampling-level ranking using automatic rerankers. We'll pair automatic scores with human spot checks. We'll accept your eval harness or run ours; both work.
[06:52] Samir: Ok, sounds thorough. Any limitations we should know about?
[06:58] Leo: A few edge cases: extremely low-latency sub-50ms workloads are challenging across shared hosted tiers; kernel determinism for some quantized formats can differ slightly; and extremely long context windows need bespoke memory configs. We'll call these out in the POC plan.
[07:14] Ethan: If we need to replicate sampling hyperparams exactly for AB tests, is there a way to lock seeds and runtime?
[07:21] Leo: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can enable determinism modes and seed control; hosted has less strict determinism but we can approximate.
[07:30] [brief silence]
[07:33] Maya: Time for quick recap and agree next steps. So Redwood will: share SOC2 + security and KMS integration doc, Leo will prepare parity benchmark plan and required eval corpus, Maya will send POC scope + pricing and propose a 2-week initial sprint. Equator will: share eval corpus and network diagram, Hannah send compliance checklist specifics. Do we all agree?
[07:55] Priya: Yes.
[07:56] Marco: Yes, I'll send top-of-stack diagram.
[07:58] Hannah: I'll fill out the compliance notes.
[08:00] Samir: Timeline wise — if we start POC next Monday that works for us.
[08:05] Maya: Great — we'll aim to deliver POC plan by Thursday, 2027-06-10, and schedule a follow-up deep-dive on Private networking with Marco for the following week.
[08:16] [small laughter]
[08:18] Oliver: Thanks all — we'll also include a checklist for Dedicated sizing if you want to preview capacity numbers.
[08:25] Samir: Perfect. Priya and I will review the benchmark plan and send any constraints.
[08:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. Bye!
[08:33] All: Bye.

End of transcript.
